baa410dba6e0:
2 February – The Presentation of the Lord

“Where is God? Wherever He is let in...” (Father Nicolae Steinhardt)

On this great feast day I am showing you an icon with a theme that is rare in Romanian iconography.
I mean the scene of the Presentation of the Lord in the Temple.
The icon (now, of course, unavailable) was painted in our workshop five years ago (model: Nicula, second half of the 18th century).

On 2 February (40 days after His birth), the Saviour's parents performed the ritual of bringing Him to the Temple to redeem Him, as the Law of Moses required. According to the Law, the Israelites were required to bring every firstborn male to the temple and dedicate him to the Lord, a practice explained by the sparing of the Israelites' firstborn on the night they left Egypt.

937945ffe291:
15 January – Mihai Eminescu

“Choosing you as our Queen,
We kneel and pray to you:
Raise us up, and save us
From the waves that toss us;
Be a shield of strength
And a wall of salvation,
Let your adored gaze
Come down upon us,
O most pure mother
And ever-virgin,
Mary!

We, who by the saint's mercy
Cast our shadow on the earth,
Pray to the compassion
Of the Morning Star of the seas;
Hear our laments,
Queen above the angels,
Show yourself from the mists,
Sweet and clear light,
O most pure mother
And ever-virgin,
Mary!” (Prayer – Mihai Eminescu)

Together with the incomparable poet's “Prayer”, we celebrate the Day of National Culture with an icon
of the Mother of God called “the Unfading Flower” or “the Lily Flower”.
77cbb4e6b812:
• 6 January: The Baptism of the Lord (Theophany)

• "The Baptism of Christ in the Jordan is linked to the revelation of the Holy Trinity to mankind. There is no greater revelation than this, for through it the triune being of God is shown to us..." (Saint Nikolai Velimirović)

• The theme of the Baptism of the Lord, one of the great events of Christendom, also called Theophany, Epiphany or the Divine Manifestation, holds an important place in the world of the peasant icons on glass.

• The icon on glass (model from Șcheii Brașovului, 19th century) that I am showing you today is one of my early icons, painted almost 6 years ago, when I was entering the fascinating world of icons. This old icon, with its inevitable imperfections, shows Jesus Christ in a humble attitude, with His hands crossed on His chest, at the moment He is baptised by His Forerunner, the great prophet John.

• Also in a humble attitude is an angel of the Lord, holding a towel in both hands as the Lord comes out of the waters of the Jordan. From the clouds, the Holy Spirit appears in the form of a dove.
ee6d463bc518:
An icon with a dedication: Confessors of Transylvania, martyrs of the true faith.

Two priests, two monks and two free peasants. Six holy Transylvanian confessors, martyrs of the true faith of our forefathers, in an icon painted on glass: saints in whom the whole Orthodox Church of Transylvania is embodied, hierarchs and clergy, monks and hermits, ordinary believers, men and women.

The Orthodox Church of Transylvania was (over the centuries) a martyr Church. Countless were the wrongs done by the masters of Transylvania (from the 18th century on) to the Transylvanian Church (including its servants and its faithful), but many too were the valiant fighters who defended the Orthodox faith of their forefathers against the oppression of the imperial power in Vienna.

These fighters were: Oprea Miclăuș (a peasant from Săliște, near Sibiu), who suffered death for the true faith; the hieromonks Visarion Sarai and Sofronie of Cioara (near Orăștie); the priests Moise Măcinic of Sibiel and Ioan of Galeș (all five celebrated on 21 October); and Atanasie Todoran of Bichigiu, in Bistrița-Năsăud (celebrated on 12 November)

The icon was painted to order, so it is not available. It can be made again, to order.

04af70e50538:
• 23 April – «Saint George the Great Martyr», the Victory-bearer, called “the spiritual springtime”.

• One of the works painted in our workshop depicting Saint George the Great Martyr is this icon painted on glass, which we are showing you today (model: Arpașu de Sus, early 19th century)

• About the icon:

- The scene shows the soldier saint George. Born in Beirut, he was an army commander under Diocletian; he defended the Christians and was martyred in 303 AD. He is one of the most venerated saints.

- He rides a white horse, dressed in armour and a cloak, with a lance that has a cross at one end, and under the horse we see the dragon pierced by the lance. Behind the saint, on the horse's rump, sits the boy Leo of Amira with a jug in his hand, which he was taking to his master in the field when Saint George freed him from slavery to the Bulgars. In the distance are the emperor's daughter, saved from the dragon's claws, and the emperor throwing him the keys of the city.

• Joyful happy name day to all who bear the name of Saint George!🥀
d7d1296f8538:
• «Saint George is called “the spiritual springtime” because through him Christianity was greatly strengthened and renewed like a spring. That is why our Church sings so beautifully on the day of remembrance of Saint George the Great Martyr: “Come, all, let us brightly celebrate the memory of the martyr George, and crown him with spring flowers, as the one who is unconquered”» (Father Cleopa)

• The most recent icon of Saint George the Great Martyr (model: Savu Moga, Arpașu de Sus, 19th century) has been finished in time to be sent to distant lands.

• So the icon is not available. If you would like a similar icon, contact me.
